part.text: Found the bug. In `streamTrim` (src/t_stream.c:800-802), the ID deltas are stored in `int` variables, but when auto-generated IDs (epoch milliseconds) follow a manually-set small ID like `10-1`, the delta overflows a 32-bit int, corrupting the computed `currid` and causing all entries to be deleted.

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `streamTrim` (src/t_stream.c:800-803): the listpack ID deltas (`ms_delta`, `seq_delta`) were stored in 32-bit `int` variables. When a manually-provided low ID (e.g. `10-1`) is followed by auto-generated epoch-millisecond IDs, the delta (~1.6 billion+) overflows `int`, corrupting the computed current ID so entries above the MINID threshold were also marked deleted — wiping the whole stream.

The fix changes both variables to `int64_t`. Verification:
- `make` builds cleanly
- `unit/type/stream` test suite: all tests pass
- Manual repro of the issue scenario: XTRIM MINID now deletes only `10-1` while all 4 auto-generated entries (IDs above the threshold) remain in the stream
